verification: Every PMID resolved through NCBI E-utilities esummary (title, first author, journal, year compared) and abstracts read through efetch; one full text read through PMC (Kruglikov & Scherer 2016). Trial registrations through the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API. US labels read in full from DailyMed SPL XML (Wegovy, Zepbound, Ozempic, Mounjaro); approval dates from Drugs@FDA and the openFDA drugsfda API, with the Wegovy S-011/S-024 and Zepbound S-013 approval letters read as PDF; FDA web pages fetched live (HTTP 200). Nothing is included on the strength of a guide reference alone.
grader: Graded 2026-09-24 by the agent under Omar Saleem's delegation ("you should be able to do that from the guide"); rule set below; final review Dr. Hannah-Shmouni
gradingRule: Grade = certainty the source gives for the specific clinical statement the lesson makes, on the guides' A–D scale. A: consistent large RCTs or approval-grade evidence. B: at least one well-designed, adequately powered RCT or an independent, quality-stratified meta-analysis (either direction). C: small or sponsor-funded RCTs without independent replication, or pooled trials dominated by them. D: animal, in-vitro, mechanistic, case series, manufacturer dossiers. 'context' = history, reviews used for framing, trial registrations without results, analytical or regulatory records (regulatory records are primary for status statements, not graded for efficacy). Where the two guides disagree, the lesson states both and the claim takes the grade the primary evidence supports. Observational studies (added 2026-09-24, GRADE starting point; confirmed by Fady Hannah-Shmouni, MD FRCPC, 2026-09-24): adequately sized cohort, case-control or cross-sectional studies grade C for the association they measured; small or single-centre ones grade D; any causal claim drawn from observational data grades D. Meta-analyses of observational studies grade at most B, and only for association. Guidelines and consensus statements are 'context', cited for what they recommend, not graded as evidence.

claims.text: Whether GLP-1 receptor agonists act directly on facial fat or dermal cells, independent of weight loss, rests on cell and animal studies and has not been tested in people.
claims.reviewNote: A&RE ch.12 calls this 'an open, actively studied question' — agrees
claims.gradeDecision: D — mechanistic hypothesis; open question

claims.text: In the US, compounded, counterfeit and falsely labelled 'research' semaglutide and tirzepatide are not FDA-approved, and FDA has warned about each (page current 1 September 2026); semaglutide bought online without a prescription has failed independent testing.
claims.reviewNote: no dosing or storage content reproduced from the FDA page
claims.gradeDecision: regulatory record + adjacent analytical evidence

claims.text: Management of facial change during incretin therapy is counselling before treatment (the Hormonaly guide advises raising facial volume and laxity, especially with older patients), monitoring with consented photographs, support for protein intake and resistance training to protect lean mass (guide advice), and referral to a qualified aesthetic clinician for restoration. Published restoration advice is expert opinion (the main consensus statement was developed with industry involvement), and randomized filler and device trials in these patients have no results yet. Decisions about the medicine belong to the prescriber and patient.
claims.reviewNote: A&RE's titration and protein-per-kg advice is excluded by the lock (finding 5)
claims.gradeDecision: D — guide advice and expert consensus; framed as counselling, monitoring and referral

claims.text: Inflammaging is chronic, low-grade, sterile inflammation that rises with age; raised inflammatory markers such as IL-6 and CRP predict morbidity, disability, frailty and death in older adults. Increased gut permeability is one proposed source.
claims.reviewNote: framing; benefit of modulating inflammation outside CVD remains controversial (Ferrucci & Fabbri)
claims.gradeDecision: context — concept and prognostic association

claims.text: Metabolic endotoxaemia is shown in mice (high-fat feeding raises plasma LPS; LPS infusion reproduces weight gain and insulin resistance) and as a transient rise in plasma endotoxin after a high-fat meal in 12 healthy men. Measuring intestinal permeability is complex, a leading review concludes it is unproven that restoring barrier function improves gastrointestinal or systemic disease, and a widely used commercial zonulin ELISA does not detect zonulin. Whether a leaky gut drives skin disease in people has not been shown.
claims.reviewNote: mechanism and human evidence taught in separate sentences
claims.gradeDecision: D — mouse + small human physiology; absence statement per Camilleri 2019

claims.text: In a Cochrane review of 39 RCTs (2,599 participants), probiotics probably make little or no difference to patient-rated eczema symptoms, and the combined severity score fell by less than the minimum clinically important difference; a 2024 EAACI meta-analysis of 20 RCTs in children without food allergy reported a significant SCORAD reduction. Probiotic effects are strain-specific.
claims.reviewNote: both directions shown; A&RE rates probiotics C generally
claims.gradeDecision: B for little or no patient-noticeable benefit (Cochrane); C for the children's pooled gain

claims.text: Other gut- and metabolism-directed skin evidence: rosacea improved after rifaximin eradication of small-intestinal bacterial overgrowth in a small single-centre RCT (C); an 8-week placebo-controlled RCT of liraglutide in 20 people with psoriasis found no effect (C); an open-label, manufacturer-sponsored phase 3b RCT (274 people) found more complete psoriasis clearance when tirzepatide was added to ixekizumab (C), and tirzepatide has no psoriasis indication in the US. A fibre-rich diet has strong human evidence for cardiometabolic outcomes (A&RE A; the review's own certainty moderate) and no skin-outcome trials; an Akkermansia pilot RCT in 32 adults improved insulin sensitivity (C). A&RE grades the 'leaky gut' repair stack (L-glutamine, zinc carnosine, BPC-157) D, and as of September 2026 BPC-157 is not on the US 503A bulks list after the July 2026 PCAC review.
claims.reviewNote: grades shown per item in the quick-fire why lines
claims.gradeDecision: C for each skin trial; B (course rule) / A (guide) for fibre's metabolic outcomes; D for the repair stack

authorFindings: Grading-rule gap — the rule has no tier for observational human studies (cohorts, surveys, imaging series, tissue biochemistry). Module 03 followed GRADE's starting point: adequately sized observational studies graded C for the association they measured, small or uncontrolled studies D, and any causal inference drawn from association D. Suggest adding this line to the rule for all modules.

A&RE ch.13 glycation paragraph — rates AGE cross-linking → loss of elasticity GRADE B and AGE–RAGE → NF-κB inflammatory signalling GRADE B, citing two reviews (Gkogkolou & Böhm 2012; Chaudhuri 2018). Gkogkolou & Böhm conclude that 'still little is known on the precise role of AGEs during skin aging'. The primary human evidence found is observational accumulation (Dyer 1993; Verzijl 2000). The course grades accumulation C and the causal skin-ageing link D, and names the disagreement; the author may wish to revisit the B.

SURMOUNT-1 figure — A&RE prints '~21%' at the top dose (the trial's treatment-regimen estimand, −20.9%) and PPG-Aug prints '22.5%' (the efficacy estimand). Both are correct for different estimands; each guide should name its estimand. The course uses the primary treatment-regimen figures (−15.0% to −20.9% vs −3.1%).

A&RE ch.12 telogen effluvium GRADE B — the anchor is a review (Persson 2025). The primary evidence is the US labels' placebo-controlled hair-loss rates (Wegovy 3.3% vs 1%, higher at the higher approved dose; Zepbound 4–5% vs 1%; mostly women; associated with weight reduction). Suggest citing the labels; the telogen-effluvium mechanism itself is inferred from observational reports.

A&RE ch.12 counselling box — 'slower titration and a gradual rate of loss reduce both lean-mass and facial-volume loss': no primary study was found linking titration pace to facial volume, and titration and the protein g/kg figure are outside the source lock. The course teaches counselling, monitoring and referral only.

A&RE ch.11–12 say rapid loss depletes 'subcutaneous and dermal fat'. The only quantitative facial study (Sharma 2025, n=20) measured superficial and deep midface compartments; no human study measuring dermal white adipose tissue on incretins was found. Suggest 'subcutaneous facial fat' unless a dermal study is cited. Relatedly, A&RE ch.11 presents dWAT's antimicrobial defence without noting it is mouse data (human acne-lesion data now exist: O'Neill 2022).

PPG-Aug semaglutide and tirzepatide entries — no skin or facial notes, although both US labels now list hair loss among common adverse reactions and the Wegovy label lists dysesthesia (altered skin sensation). The semaglutide entry's indications omit the March 2024 cardiovascular risk-reduction indication (Wegovy S-011, SELECT). The current Mounjaro label (effective 27 August 2026) includes a cardiovascular risk-reduction indication that the August build does not list.

A&RE ch.16 grades a fibre-rich diet A; the review it cites (Reynolds 2019) rates certainty 'moderate' for dietary fibre and has no skin outcomes, which the course rule maps to B. The course reports the guide's A for metabolic outcomes, states the review's certainty, and says no trial has measured skin.

A&RE ch.12 'small studies report improvement in psoriasis GRADE C' — still C, but two primary trials now bracket it: a negative 20-patient placebo-controlled RCT of liraglutide (Faurschou 2015) and an open-label, Lilly-sponsored phase 3b RCT of tirzepatide added to ixekizumab (Lebwohl 2026, TOGETHER-PsO). Worth citing both.

Not in either guide, worth adding — Sharma 2025 (first quantitative imaging of midface volume on GLP-1 RAs), Rao 2026 (1,226-patient survey: facial and hair effects rise with weight lost), Batsis 2026 (independent review of body composition across 35 RCTs), the Cochrane review of probiotics for eczema (Makrgeorgou 2018), Scheffler 2018 (commercial zonulin ELISA does not detect zonulin), and the US labels as the primary source for hair-loss rates.

Reference check — every A&RE reference the module uses from chapters 11, 12, 13, 14 and 16 (Kershaw & Flier; Zhang 2015; Chen 2019; SELECT; Drucker; STEP-1; SURMOUNT-1; Camilleri; Burke; Persson; Franceschi 2000; Ferrucci & Fabbri; Gkogkolou & Böhm; Chaudhuri; Humphrey & Lawrence; Conte; Reynolds; Suez; Depommier) resolved on PubMed with the printed journal, volume and year. PPG-Aug PMIDs for STEP-1, SURMOUNT-1, SELECT and SURMOUNT-OSA resolve.

Jurisdiction — both guides are US-centred for incretin regulation; module 03 asserts US status only (FDA labels, Drugs@FDA, FDA statement current 1 September 2026). MHRA/EMA status of Wegovy, Mounjaro and compounded GLP-1 products is not asserted and needs mapping for UK learners (in progress).
